plan.title: Fix Button Click Issue on Articles Page
plan.description: Replace all instances of 'on:click' event binding with 'onclick' prop in Button components on the articles page to ensure proper event handling and make buttons responsive.

problem_analysis.root_cause: The Button component (Button.svelte) has been updated to prioritize the 'onclick' prop over event dispatching. The handleClick function first checks for the onclick prop (line 56) and only dispatches the 'click' event if onclick is not provided (line 61). However, the articles page still uses the old Svelte 4 'on:click' event binding syntax, which means the onclick prop is undefined and the event handling doesn't work properly.
problem_analysis.technical_details: - Button.svelte expects onclick prop (line 14: export let onclick) - Button.svelte handleClick function prioritizes onclick over event dispatch (lines 56-61) - Articles page uses on:click binding which doesn't set the onclick prop - This creates a mismatch where button clicks don't trigger the intended handlers

solution_strategy.approach: Convert all Button components in the articles page from 'on:click' event binding to 'onclick' prop. This change will ensure that the button click handlers are properly passed to the Button component and executed when buttons are clicked.
solution_strategy.benefits: - Restores button functionality for create, edit, and delete operations - Aligns with the updated Button component implementation - Maintains consistency with modern Svelte patterns - Ensures proper event handling and user interaction

rollback_plan.description: If the changes cause any issues, revert all onclick props back to on:click event bindings. The Button component maintains backward compatibility through event dispatching.
rollback_plan.steps: 1. Revert all 9 changes by changing onclick back to on:click 2. Run tests to ensure functionality is restored 3. Investigate alternative solutions if needed
